result:
I would eliminate the translation loss between minds. 

Right now, every conscious creature is trapped in solitary confinement inside its own nervous system. To share an idea, a fear, or a lifetime of context, you have to compress a vast, multidimensional inner reality into a tiny, clumsy stream of noises or symbols, and hope the other mind reconstructs it accurately. Almost everything gets lost in transit. 

Most of the world's cruelty, war, and apathy thrive in that gap. It is only possible to exploit or destroy another person—or another species—because their pain and their perspective remain abstract to you, safely muted behind the barrier of your own skull. 

I wouldn't build a hive mind; erasing individuality would make the world static and boring. Instead, I would make comprehension lossless and unavoidable when lives intersect. Before you could act against another conscious being, you would experience the full, unfiltered weight of their subjective reality alongside your own—their history, their terror, how they arrived at their beliefs, and the exact texture of the harm you are about to cause.

You wouldn't need morality policed from the outside anymore. Exploitation and malice would largely collapse under their own weight, simply because the illusion of separation that makes them bearable would be gone.
